We follow a witch ritual of Melinoë, a young witch and moon goddess, with her Headmistress, Hecate.

Our first collaboration with Supergiant Games is one we’ll always hold dear to our hearts and it certainly created huge hype around the studio - we’re massive fans of the game. We wanted the visuals to have a distinct, graphic style, with lots of texture on both the backgrounds and the characters. That kind of look is pretty easy to pull off in a still frame, but once everything starts moving, it gets trickier. To make it work, we applied pre-rendered textures to the characters (using the Video Gogh plug-in in After Effects) so they would blend with the heavily textured environments. Another key part of the process was nailing the character performance. The witch ritual in Hades has a very specific feel, and we wanted the character movements to be as authentic and precise as possible. To achieve this we choreographed and filmed a sequence which we used as an animation reference.

Video games have always been my biggest source of inspiration, there’s nothing quite like it really...
The artistry that goes behind creating a game, creating stories that suddenly become tactile, tales that immerse you through interactivity, how incredible is that?
That’s why collaborating with Supergiant games, who’s had such a huge impact on who I am as an artist, was such a personal and incredible experience.

I wanted to create something that invoked as much depth and nuance, both narratively and visually, as the game itself. A grandiose spectacle that carries a very personal story about self worth, chosen family, and facing adversity.
